title: Ethernet: CRCStripTypePacket does not work Stm32H7S3L8 NUCLEO
body:
Hello everyone, I have the following use case: I want to receive raw data via Ethernet, which works fine, but I have a problem: When I send 100 bytes, I only receive 14 bytes in my software on the MCU (STM32H7S3L8). I was able to fix this by setting
AutomaticPadCRCStrip to DISABLE. Now I receive 104 bytes, which is also not the desired behavior. After a little research, I found out that the 4 bytes are CRC, so I continued searching. After some searching, I found the CRCStripTypePacket property and set it to ENABLE, but unfortunately this property has no effect. What do I need to do to get my 100 bytes but not the CRC? Do I need to set something else? Is this a bug? Please help me, I'm stuck.

Legitimate Ethernet frames work, but I want to use my own protocol without the Ethernet header in front of it.

I am asking for help with the setup so that my data arrives as it was sent. Here is a link to the stm32 forum where I already asked the question. 

https://community.st.com/t5/stm32-mcus-embedded-software/raw-ethernet-how-can-i-remove-the-crc-upon-receipt/m-p/863127#M70863

Thank you very much,

stm32h7rsxx-hal-driver 1.2.1

title: SDIO HAL ReadExtended / WriteExtended does not calculate number of blocks correctly
body:
The HAL driver in functions `HAL_SDIO_ReadExtended()` and `HAL_SDIO_WriteExtended()` does not calculate number of blocks to read / write correctly.

The code in question is: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7rsxx-hal-driver/blob/580b47200c8d757a72ecfc38abb59f9db7041a29/Src/stm32h7rsxx_hal_sdio.c#L976
The same code is used in other read / write functions.

The calculated block number will only be correct for the case `size == block size`. 
It should be possible to send data with different length than multiple of block size (I haven't seen any limitation noted in that regard).

Here are a few example results of calculating number of blocks with this code:
- `Size_byte=512`, `hsdio->block_size=512` -> `nbr_of_block=1` : OK
- `Size_byte=510`, `hsdio->block_size=512` -> `nbr_of_block=0` : NOT OK, expected 1
- `Size_byte=513`, `hsdio->block_size=512` -> `nbr_of_block=1` : NOT OK, expected 2
- `Size_byte=2048`, `hsdio->block_size=512` -> `nbr_of_block=4` :  OK
- `Size_byte=2049`, `hsdio->block_size=512` -> `nbr_of_block=4` : NOT_OK, expected 5

We can see that the calculated size is true only when `size_byte` is a multiple of `hsdio->block_size=512`, otherwise the calculated number of blocks is  1 block to small.
Example of correct calculation of block size:
```
/* Assuming block mode, minimum 1-block to send */
nbr_of_blocks = 1;
while(Size_byte > hsdio->block_size) {
   nbr_of_blocks++;
   Size_byte -= hsdio->block_size;
}
```

comments.author: MaroMetelski
comments.body:
On a second thought I may be in the wrong about supporting writing / reading of data that's not multiple of block size in block mode. I think if there is no hardware or SDMMC LL driver limitation it's a valid use case. That would allow to send data payloads larger than 512 bytes (limitation of byte mode) without allocating extra large buffers in the application).
But I think there may be more changes need in order to make that work, for example adjusting this:
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7rsxx-hal-driver/blob/580b47200c8d757a72ecfc38abb59f9db7041a29/Src/stm32h7rsxx_hal_sdio.c#L994

comments.author: MKISTM
comments.body:
Hello @MaroMetelski,

Thank you for your report.

After analyzing the issue and returning to the STM32H7 reference manual [RM0477](https://www.st.com/resource/en/reference_manual/rm0477-stm32h7rx7sx-armbased-32bit-mcus-stmicroelectronics.pdf) we found that this behavior is expected.

In the RM at SDMMC registers section, the description of the SDMMC data length register (SDMMC_DLENR) this register contains the number of data bytes to be transferred, Regarding the bits descriptions:
> When DDR = 1 DATALENGTH is truncated to a multiple of 2. (The last odd byte is not transferred)
> Note: For a block data transfer, the value in the data length register must be a multiple of the block size (see SDMMC_DCTRL). 

Looking at SDMMC_DCTRL, the description of the DBLOCKSIZE bits:
> When DATALENGTH is not a multiple of DBLOCKSIZE, the transferred data is truncated at a multiple of DBLOCKSIZE. (None of the remaining data are transferred.)
> When DDR = 1, DBLOCKSIZE = 0000 must not be used. (No data are transfered)

These descriptions explain the expected behavior mentioned in your report above: 
- `Size_byte=510`, `hsdio->block_size=512` -> `nbr_of_block=0` 
- `Size_byte=513`, `hsdio->block_size=512` -> `nbr_of_block=1` 
- `Size_byte=2049`, `hsdio->block_size=512` -> `nbr_of_block=4`


Please let us know if you encounter any specific unexpected behavior or errors, and we will be happy to assist further.

BR,
Mohamed Chaker.

comments.author: MKISTM
comments.body:
Hello @MaroMetelski,

If you don't have any update or feedback, please allow to close this issue.
We appreciate you're understanding.

BR,
Mohamed Chaker.

comments.author: MaroMetelski
comments.body: Hey @MKISTM . Sorry for the late response. I think we can close the issue. Thanks for the clarification and sources. I think I jumped to conclusions a bit too quickly :)

title: Overflow when transmitting SPI data
body:
HAL_SPI_TransmitReceive gives a timeout in polling mode.

When transmitting over SPI5 we get a timeout on transmitting upon sending a large dataset (4096 bytes).
SPI5 is configured as a Master, 2 Line device, transmit and receive data in 8 Bit mode.

Not in every loop the SPI_FLAG_RXP is set, so no data is read. This will cause a discrepancy in the TxXferCount and RxXferCount and therefor a Timeout after the /* Timeout management */

When setting a breakpoint on the corresponding SPI_CloseTransfer we also see SPI_FLAG_OVR is set. 
However when checking for the SPI_FLAG_OVR in the loop, this is never set and will transmit all bytes successfully. A tiny delay might seem to be the solution. Since the function is polling, a wait for SPI_FLAG_TXP might be a solution

Clock settings:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1cb4e210-7b37-43a1-98ef-aea451065fd3)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26590aa5-843e-4c20-a185-fdf0fc121bc3)

comments.author: rgqsch
comments.body:
We work with the STM32H7S7I8 running at a SYSCLK of 600Mhz.
The code is running from external RAM bus speed 100MHz, DTR enabled - 8 bit wide
ICache as well as DCache is enabled

We initialize the SPI 5 peripheral as follows:
Peripheral clock 150MHz
BaudRatePrescaler 2 (SPI master clock/8 so outgoing clock @ ~19MHz)
SPI_MODE_MASTER; // Set the mode to SPI master
SPI_DIRECTION_2LINES; // Set the mode to 2 lines full duplex
SPI_DATASIZE_8BIT; // Set the data size to 8 bit

It might be that the peripheral is too fast for the external code to load? I will run a test with the peripheral clock at a lower speed

title: Ethernet HAL driver definitions
body:
I did some comparisons between the new STM32H7RS HAL Driver V1.1.0 and STM32H7xx HAL Driver V1.11.4 and I found this:

File `stm32h7rsxx_hal_eth.h`
``` c
#define HAL_ETH_STATE_BUSY                 0x00000023U    /*!< an internal process is ongoing             */
#define HAL_ETH_STATE_STARTED              0x00000023U    /*!< an internal process is started             */
```

File `stm32h7xx_hal_eth.h`
``` c
#define HAL_ETH_STATE_BUSY                 0x00000020U    /*!< an internal process is ongoing             */
#define HAL_ETH_STATE_STARTED              0x00000040U    /*!< an internal process is started             */
```

title: Problematic macro definition in stm32h7rsxx_ll_adc.h
body:
Hello,

There seems to be some problem with the macro definitions VREFINT_CAL_ADDR, TEMPSENSOR_CAL1_ADDR and TEMPSENSOR_CAL2_ADDR in the stm32h7rsxx_ll_adc.h file
```C
#define VREFINT_CAL_ADDR                   ((uint16_t*) (0x1FF1E810UL))
#define TEMPSENSOR_CAL1_ADDR               ((uint16_t*) (0x1FF1E814UL))
#define TEMPSENSOR_CAL2_ADDR               ((uint16_t*) (0x1FF1E818UL)) 
```

According to the description in the datasheet, it should be defined as follows
```C
#define VREFINT_CAL_ADDR                   ((uint16_t*) (0x08FFF810UL))
#define TEMPSENSOR_CAL1_ADDR               ((uint16_t*) (0x08FFF814UL))
#define TEMPSENSOR_CAL2_ADDR               ((uint16_t*) (0x08FFF818UL)) 
```

comments.author: RJMSTM
comments.body: ST Internal Reference: 182742

title: Missing ifdefs in stm32h7rsxx_util_i3c.c
body:
Hello,

The file `stm32h7rsxx_util_i3c.c` does not have the `#ifdef HAL_I3C_MODULE_ENABLED`  that the other HAL components have, which leads to undefined symbols when we compile with I3C module disabled.  Same goes for its corresponding header file if we add the ifdef in the `stm32h7rsxx_util_i3c.c` file after the include (it seems to be done that way in the other sources).

comments.author: KRASTM
comments.body:
Hello @opkaizen,

Thank you for the report.

The `#ifdef HAL_xxx_MODULE_ENABLED` used in all HAL component, but the file `stm32h7rsxx_util_i3c.c` it is a helper that contain 2 functions for computation of different timing parameter as mentioned in the brief at the top of the file **"This utility help to calculate the different I3C Timing"**. In other word an extra file could be included when needed, if I3C module used and enabled, with HAL_DRIVER or FULL_LL_DRIVER.

with regards,

comments.author: opkaizen
comments.body:
Hello @KRASTM,
I understand this is not directly linked to the I3C module implementation but it is using its symbols, which means we cannot include all the C files as sources in our compilation base if this define is not added.

To give an example of the current issue :
- I'm compiling all C files, whether I'm using all the modules or not
- I don't have to use I3C, so I don't define HAL_I3C_MODULE_ENABLED in the HAL configuration header
- My compiler will say the `stm32h7rsxx_util_i3c.c` has undefined symbols

The workaround could be to force your users to exclude this particular file from the compilation if they don't use it, but it seems to be exactly what these ifdefs are for, aren't they?

comments.author: KRASTM
comments.body:
Hello @opkaizen,

You are right, despite that the file is linked to I3C module and it makes no sense to use it without I3C enabled. But we should add the `#ifdef HAL_I3C_MODULE_ENABLED` to prevent those error.

With regards,

comments.author: KRASTM
comments.body: ST Internal Reference: 182462

comments.author: KRASTM
comments.body:
Hello @opkaizen,

The issue you reported has been fixed in the frame of version v1.1.0 of the STM32CubeH7RS HAL Driver published recently on GitHub. Thank you again for having reported.

With regards.
